text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Latvia has given up the disputed region of Abrene as Latvian and Russian delegations agree on a draft border delimitation treaty. Some sectors of the border are still to be agreed upon. The next meeting of delegations is due March 20 and 21 in Riga.
- Proposed new minister of finance, Roberts Zile, is likely to be approved by parliament today following the approval by the government parties on Wednesday.

- Deputies Ilga Kreituse, former parliament chairman, and Aivars Kreituss, former finance minister, announced plans to set up a new party, The Labour party. It says it will defend the interests of employees and is expected to be supported by industrialists and some intellectuals.

- Deputy prime minister Juris Kaksitis, accused by political opponents of having convicted a Latvian dissident in 1986 when being member of the High Court, has admitted his fault. At the same time he claimed having acquitted scores of dissidents.
- The director-general of the state revenue service, Andrejs Sonchiks, overruled an order to close five customs check points in Riga port, issued by Riga customs chief.
- Welfare Minister Vladimir Makarov and the co-ordinator of the UNDP in Latvia, John Hendra, signed a project for co-operation in the field of the people's reproductive health.
- President Ulmanis suggests the current pension law be revised.
- President Ulmanis has considered 129 petitions for clemency, of which only 10 have been accepted.

- Russian vice-premier Valery Serov, co-chairman of the Latvian-Russian joint commission, is due to arrive in Riga. The Russian delegation will also include a vice-president of Lukoil, which means that the agenda of talks will also include questions related to the export of Russian oil and Ventspils port.
- On March 4-7 Riga will host the Polish Expo '97 trade fair.
- Riga meat packing plant has found new partners in Russia and is preparing to increase its exports to Russia.
- Mesa Housing Industries, one of Turkey's largest building companies, is planning to build a modern trade centre and a recreation centre in Riga by investing about $40 million.
